findings.element: owner-empty, the answered frame — act("Add a moment", true, { "data-act": "add" }) at render-b.js:1209
findings.problem: Round 5 asked for a second frame and it was built, but the only control on it does nothing. Driven: type 3 October 2026, press Set the day, and the frame replaces itself with the horizon, the date and one primary button reading Add a moment — which is then focused (render-b.js:1213-1214). Pressing it once changes nothing. Pressing it twice changes nothing: zero .b-item rows appear, no editor opens, the reversibility bar stays silent, the hint under it still reads "The day is set. Moments come next." The button is a real, enabled button with data-primary=true, but this state's only click handler returns early unless the target is [data-act="setday"] (render-b.js:1184), and the add handler at line 919 belongs to the owner-flight node. So the owner's very first action in the product is a dead control, and the product's own stated rule — anything not built has no button element — is broken in the one place a first-timer meets it. Everything after this point works: rename, hide, move, delete and undo all fire. The single journey that turns a stranger into an owner is the only one that does not run.
findings.fix: In the setday branch of render-b.js (the block ending at line 1215), after replacing .b-empty with next, bind the same delegated handler the owner state uses: next.addEventListener("click", function (event) { if (!event.target.closest('[data-act="add"]')) return; add one untitled moment dated midway between today and the day, then re-render into the owner state with that moment's editor open and its title field focused }) — the same landing the owner-flight Add produces today. If crossing into the owner-flight fixture is not wanted, re-render owner-empty's own node with the one row plus the editor instead; either way the press must produce a row, an open editor, and a reversibility line reading "A moment was added." Assert it in interaction-check.mjs: from owner-empty, answering the day and pressing the primary must raise the item count from 0 to 1, open exactly one editor, and put the undo control in its live state.

findings.element: owner-empty, the answered frame — countBlock(away) and .b-when at render-b.js:1202-1204
findings.problem: The answered frame renders "79 / DAYS / Saturday 3 October 2026" and never states what today is. Every other surface in the product carries the rule — owner-flight, owner-editing, phone, desk and loading all print TODAY IS 16 JULY, and the loading frame prints it before it has anything else to say. Here the one figure on screen is a subtraction from a date the reader is never given, on the exact screen where the reader has the least context: they have typed one date, they have never seen this product before, and the first thing it does is show them a number it will not explain. This is the unanchored-time class from the defect library returning on the newest surface — the class was paid for once, and the state that reintroduces it is a state nobody screenshots, so no frame in the panel's list shows it.
findings.fix: In the next node at render-b.js:1201, insert the same today rule the owner state builds, between .b-when and .b-emptyBody, reading the date from the fixture clock through the existing accessor rather than a new string — the same element, class and ink the owner surface uses, so the two frames are the same object. Then extend interaction-check.mjs's anchor assertion to cover this state: any frame that renders a figure or a date must also render the today rule exactly once, checked across all eleven states plus the answered first run.

findings.element: the Behind you disclosure on owner-flight and owner-editing (behindBlock, render-b.js:294-420)
findings.problem: Opening Behind you on the owner's own surface yields three rows and zero controls — driven, the details element contains no button, link or field at all. The deliberate decision that where the past is listed there is no control is right for a guest, who has nothing to do with it; applied to the owner it means every moment they enter becomes permanently uneditable the day after it passes. Over the nine months this fixture spans, that is the entire plan: a typo in a supplier's name, a moment marked Not going ahead that is back on, a date entered a week wrong and noticed later — none can be corrected, and there is no route from the past back into the measure. The product also asks the owner to trust it with the record: the guest sheet, the keepsake and the wedding-morning screen all draw the past, and the morning screen is nine-tenths past. The owner is shown a record they will be judged on and cannot amend.
findings.fix: Keep the guest past exactly as it is, and give the owner's copy one control per row and nothing more: make each .b-behindRow on an owner surface the same full-row Edit target the measure already uses, with the accessible name "Edit <title>. <weekday> <date>, <n> days back. <shown/hidden>." It opens the existing editor unchanged — the date field and the -7/-1/+1/+7 controls already handle a date in the past, and a date moved forward past today returns the moment to the measure, which is correct and already animated. Do not add a second editor and do not add controls to the fold's summary sentence. Assert in interaction-check.mjs that on owner surfaces every past row is one focusable target, that no guest surface has any, and that a past moment re-dated ahead of today leaves Behind you, appears on the measure, and is named by the reversibility bar.

findings.element: owner-empty, the day field and Set the day (render-b.js:1170-1180); the stage contains no form element
findings.problem: The first screen of the product is a single labelled text field with a single button beside it. Typing a date and pressing Enter — the reflex of everyone who has ever filled in a field — does nothing at all: no submit, no validation, no announcement, no visible change. Driven at 1440 and confirmed against the source: the stage contains zero form elements, so the field has no implicit submission and the button is a click handler only. For the named audience, someone who has never used a tool of this kind, a field that swallows Enter in silence is indistinguishable from a product that is broken, and it happens before they have seen anything the product is good at. The same reflex is handled correctly everywhere else: Enter in the editor's title field leaves the editor open with the rename already committed live.
findings.fix: Wrap the field and the button in a real form element at render-b.js:1170 and move the existing setday branch onto its submit event (form.addEventListener("submit", function (e) { e.preventDefault(); ... })), leaving the button as type=submit so click and Enter run one code path. The invalid branches at lines 1216-1222 then answer Enter with the same three sentences they answer a click with. Assert in interaction-check.mjs that pressing Enter in the day field with a valid date produces the answered frame, and that an empty or unreadable value produces the same aria-invalid state and the same wording a press of the button produces.

findings.element: ended state body copy — "The day was Saturday 3 October 2026. Orla can send a new link."
findings.problem: The ended surface is the one screen a guest reaches with a live need: they have the plan open on a phone, it has stopped working, and they want it back. It answers with a sentence about a third party — Orla can send a new link. Orla is named nowhere else on the guest's screen except in mono micro-type at the foot (KEPT BY ORLA), is never introduced as a person or a role, and the sentence describes an action only she can take with no way for the reader to ask for it. Read by someone who was sent this link by a family member, it is an instruction addressed to a person who is not in the room. The empty-state rule from the defect library — one true first move, stated once — is the rule this screen misses: it states a fact and offers no move, and it is the only screen in the product where that is true.
findings.fix: Rewrite the second line to address the reader and name the move they can make: "Ask Orla, who keeps this plan, for a new link." Keep the first and third sentences verbatim. Where the fixture carries the keeper's contact, make that name the one control on the screen, as a real mailto or tel link labelled "Ask Orla for a new link"; where it does not, leave it as the sentence with no button, which stays consistent with the rule that nothing unbuilt gets a button. Assert in interaction-check.mjs that the ended state names the keeper in the body and not only in the foot, and that the same name string is used in both places.

biggestWin: One thing holds this seat below 9.5 and it is the owner's first five minutes: the first run is a pair of still frames rather than a flow, because the answered empty project shows a count without ever saying what today is and then hands the owner a focused primary button that does nothing at all, so the only journey that turns a stranger into an owner is the only one in the product that does not run — everything downstream of it (the measure, the docked editor, the reversibility bar that names its key and falls silent, the preview, the publish ceremony, and above all the guest phone surface, which reads in about four seconds and is the best object here) is finished work.
